questions.question: What vessel-wall features constitute brain arteriolosclerosis, and which should remain separate constructs?
questions.index_or_exposure: Hyalinosis, sclerosis, fibrosis, wall thickening, luminal narrowing, smooth-muscle loss
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: The label is heterogeneous and operational definitions vary.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Consensus construct ontology linked to reproducible quantitative measurements.
questions.decisive_design: Multicentre digital-pathology calibration with shared slides and blinded raters

questions.question: How should regional arteriolosclerosis measurements be aggregated into a person-level burden?
questions.comparator: Maximum, mean, weighted, latent, and spatial-pattern scores
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: No universally accepted aggregation rule exists.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Sampling theory for spatially heterogeneous disease.
questions.decisive_design: Dense multiregion sampling with bootstrap stability and external outcome validation

questions.question: What minimum MRI protocol is required to phenotype hemorrhagic and nonhemorrhagic cSVD reproducibly?
questions.index_or_exposure: T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, susceptibility, and optional quantitative sequences
questions.reference_standard: STRIVE-aligned acquisition and expert image review
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Core structural and susceptibility-sensitive sequences are necessary, but protocol effects remain substantial.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Prospective sequence-ablation evidence across scanners.
questions.decisive_design: Multivendor scan-rescan study with blinded sequence-ablation reading

questions.question: Which cSVD measures are repeatable enough for longitudinal or treatment-response use?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Some tools are repeatable, but repeatability does not imply biological or clinical validity.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Common change thresholds and error decomposition.
questions.decisive_design: Multisite scan-rescan plus longitudinal progression study

questions.question: How accurately does Boston v2.0 identify CAA in symptomatic referral populations?
questions.population: Age 50+ with ICH, TFNE, or cognitive presentation
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Performance is strongest in populations resembling the derivation and symptomatic validation cohorts.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Independent prospective validation with uniform full reference standards.
questions.decisive_design: Prospective multicentre blinded diagnostic cohort

questions.question: How accurately does Boston v2.0 perform in nonhemorrhagic cognitive presentations?
questions.population: Memory-clinic or cognitive presentations without hemorrhage
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Available validation suggests substantially weaker performance than in symptomatic hemorrhagic cohorts.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Larger representative pathology-linked cohorts.
questions.decisive_design: Prospective memory-clinic-to-autopsy validation with competing AD pathology

questions.question: Can Boston v2.0 be used for community screening?
questions.comparator: No screening or alternative risk model
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Community sensitivity is limited and predictive values depend strongly on prevalence.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Prospective population-based evaluation and consequences of false classification.
questions.decisive_design: Population screening study with autopsy follow-up and decision analysis

questions.question: Does cortical versus juxtacortical microbleed localization improve CAA specificity?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Histopathology suggests some false-positive lobar lesions arise from nonamyloid arteriolosclerosis.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Automated reproducible localization and prospective pathology validation.
questions.decisive_design: Lesion-matched MRI-histology study with competing arteriolosclerosis

questions.question: How should cortical superficial siderosis extent and progression be used for prognosis?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: cSS is associated with recurrence risk, but treatment decisions require absolute and context-specific risk.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Calibrated external models and treatment interaction evidence.
questions.decisive_design: Prospective competing-risk cohort with prespecified cSS progression

questions.question: Does severe centrum semiovale PVS add independent diagnostic information for CAA?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: CSO-PVS contributes to Boston v2.0 and spatial pathology evidence supports biological relevance.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Large external pathology-linked incremental-value study.
questions.decisive_design: Blinded MRI-autopsy cohort with model comparison

questions.question: Is the multispot WMH pattern independently informative for CAA?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: It contributes to Boston v2.0, but independent validation remains limited.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Standardized definition, reliability, and external pathology validation.
questions.decisive_design: Multicentre blinded imaging-pathology study

questions.question: When do CT morphology and APOE genotype add value after lobar ICH?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: The model can support CAA inference when MRI is unavailable, within its intended ICH context.
questions.critical_missing_piece: External validation across ancestries and modern care pathways.
questions.decisive_design: Prospective pragmatic diagnostic-impact study

questions.question: What ante-mortem MRI phenotype best predicts pathology-confirmed brain arteriolosclerosis?
questions.population: Older adults with MRI before death
questions.index_or_exposure: Deep microbleeds, lacunes, WMH topography, diffusion, physiology, and demographics
questions.comparator: Clinical vascular risks and conventional MRI burden
questions.outcome: External discrimination, calibration, and net reclassification
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: No accepted MRI diagnostic criteria exist; current features are candidate phenotypes.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Large representative MRI-autopsy derivation and locked external validation.
questions.decisive_design: Two-cohort prospective or nested autopsy prediction study

questions.question: How specific are deep microbleeds for nonamyloid arteriolosclerosis?
questions.population: Older adults with deep or mixed microbleeds
questions.index_or_exposure: Deep lesion burden and microanatomic localization
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Deep distribution is compatible with perforator disease but is not a direct pathology diagnosis.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Lesion-matched pathology with CAA and mixed-disease controls.
questions.decisive_design: Multiregion lesion-to-vessel histology study

questions.question: Which lacune locations and morphologies are most informative for arteriolosclerosis?
questions.index_or_exposure: Location, shape, cavity characteristics, and surrounding tissue
questions.reference_standard: Regional arteriolar pathology and infarct mechanism adjudication
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Lacunes are heterogeneous downstream injuries and current descriptors are not pathology-specific.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Mechanism-adjudicated spatial pathology validation.
questions.decisive_design: Prospective MRI plus autopsy or surgical histology study

questions.question: Can WMH spatial patterns distinguish arteriolosclerosis from CAA, AD, and mixed disease?
questions.index_or_exposure: Periventricular/deep pattern, shape, texture, and longitudinal expansion
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: WMH are sensitive to tissue injury but highly nonspecific.
questions.critical_missing_piece: External pathology-linked spatial model with sequence harmonization.
questions.decisive_design: Multicohort MRI-autopsy radiomics study with locked thresholds

questions.question: Does ARTS externally predict pathology-confirmed arteriolosclerosis?
questions.comparator: Demographics, vascular risks, WMH, and diffusion baselines
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: ARTS has promising development evidence but lacks strong independent pathology validation.
questions.critical_missing_piece: External locked validation outside ROSMAP-related development data.
questions.decisive_design: Independent preregistered MRI-autopsy validation

questions.question: Does ARTS add clinically meaningful information beyond conventional measures?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Associations and technical repeatability do not yet establish incremental clinical utility.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Head-to-head incremental-value and decision-curve analysis.
questions.decisive_design: External cohort with locked model and prespecified utility thresholds

questions.question: How reproducible are visual and quantitative arteriolosclerosis ratings across regions and laboratories?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Quantitative methods are emerging, but a shared calibrated reference is absent.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Public reference slide set and round-robin study.
questions.decisive_design: International blinded digital-pathology challenge

questions.question: Is impaired perivascular clearance an initiating cause, amplifier, or consequence of CAA?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Clearance impairment is coherent and spatially associated, but human direction and flux remain uncertain.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Direct human transport measurement before and during amyloid accumulation.
questions.decisive_design: Longitudinal hereditary/sporadic multimodal transport study

questions.question: Does vascular physiological dysfunction precede irreversible tissue injury?
questions.population: Individuals across preclinical and clinical SVD stages
questions.index_or_exposure: CVR, pulsatility, perfusion, and barrier measures
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: CVR can precede WMH/PVS progression in SVD, but etiologic and causal specificity remain unresolved.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Repeated physiology and imaging with causal mediation and intervention.
questions.decisive_design: Multisite longitudinal cohort with repeated measures

questions.question: Is BBB leakage an early driver of CAA and arteriolosclerosis or a downstream marker?
questions.population: Human tissue and in-vivo SVD stages
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Leakage co-localizes with vessel injury and inflammation, but temporal direction in humans is uncertain.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Prospective serial permeability imaging anchored to pathology or strong etiologic models.
questions.decisive_design: Spatial longitudinal imaging-pathology study

questions.question: Which inflammatory pathways are causal, protective, or secondary in CAA?
questions.population: Sporadic CAA, CAA-ri, ARIA, and models
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Inflammation participates in CAA-ri and ARIA; its role in non-inflammatory CAA is less defined.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Mechanistically targeted longitudinal human studies with treatment perturbation.
questions.decisive_design: Parallel CAA/CAA-ri/ARIA immune-phenotyping study

questions.question: How do pulsatility, stiffness, autoregulation, and smooth-muscle loss interact in deep perforator injury?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: A plausible network exists, but direct human causal chains are sparse.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Synchronized hemodynamics, high-resolution vessel imaging, and pathology.
questions.decisive_design: Longitudinal multimodal deep-perforator study

questions.question: Can CSF or plasma distinguish CAA from AD and mixed amyloid disease?
questions.population: CAA, AD, mixed pathology, and controls
questions.index_or_exposure: Amyloid isoforms, p-tau, GFAP, NfL, vascular markers
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: No standalone marker currently has adequate specificity and validation.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Pathology-linked multisite head-to-head assay study.
questions.decisive_design: Prospective blinded diagnostic study with locked assays

questions.question: Can regional amyloid PET distinguish vascular from parenchymal amyloid at the patient level?
questions.population: Suspected CAA, AD, and mixed disease
questions.index_or_exposure: Regional tracer ratios and spatial models
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Group-level regional differences exist, but pathology-specific patient thresholds are not validated.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Prospective multi-tracer PET-to-autopsy validation.
questions.decisive_design: Prespecified multicentre diagnostic study

questions.question: Which diffusion metric best captures clinically meaningful SVD microstructural injury?
questions.index_or_exposure: PSMD, free water, DTI, NODDI, and related metrics
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Several measures are reproducible and associated with cognition, but construct and etiologic specificity differ.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Head-to-head harmonized comparison with pathology and longitudinal outcomes.
questions.decisive_design: MarkVCID-style multicentre benchmark

questions.question: Are PSMD and free-water measures responsive and interpretable enough for trials?
questions.outcome: Treatment sensitivity and minimal important change
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Technical and biological validation is advancing, but treatment responsiveness is not established.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Prospective trial-embedded repeatability and responsiveness study.
questions.decisive_design: Multisite intervention study with prespecified change thresholds

questions.question: Does multimodal integration improve etiologic inference beyond MRI alone?
questions.index_or_exposure: MRI plus fluid, PET, genetics, physiology, and clinical data
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Multimodal integration is plausible but rarely tested against representative pathology.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Locked multimodal model with missing-data strategy and external validation.
questions.decisive_design: Two-stage development/validation MRI-autopsy study

questions.question: How do vascular amyloid and AD neuropathologic change interact to produce cognition?
questions.population: Older adults with autopsy and longitudinal cognition
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: The pathologies often coexist; shared amyloid biology does not imply identical compartmental effects.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Large multiregion pathology cohort with preregistered interaction and mediation models.
questions.decisive_design: Longitudinal autopsy cohort with independent replication

questions.question: How do arteriolosclerosis and CAA jointly shape MRI phenotypes and outcomes?
questions.population: Older adults with both pathologies represented
questions.index_or_exposure: Joint pathology burden and spatial distribution
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Mixed pathology is common, but many diagnostic studies simplify it as exclusion or noise.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Factorial pathology-linked imaging analysis with sufficient dual-pathology cases.
questions.decisive_design: Multicohort MRI-autopsy interaction study

questions.question: What links arteriolosclerosis to hippocampal sclerosis and LATE-related pathology?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Associations exist, but shared age, vascular injury, and selective vulnerability remain competing explanations.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Longitudinal and spatial mediation with replication.
questions.decisive_design: Independent multiregion autopsy cohorts

questions.question: How much cognitive decline is mediated by infarcts, white-matter injury, network disruption, and neurodegeneration?

questions.current_answer: Multiple pathways likely operate simultaneously; simple adjusted regressions may obscure them.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Temporal causal models with measurement-error correction and sensitivity analysis.
questions.decisive_design: Harmonized longitudinal multimodal autopsy cohort

questions.question: Which findings from hereditary CAA transport to sporadic CAA?
questions.index_or_exposure: Shared imaging, fluid, physiology, and pathology measures
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Hereditary CAA is mechanistically informative but differs in age, mutation, penetrance, and co-pathology.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Direct parallel phenotyping with formal transport analysis.
questions.decisive_design: Matched hereditary-sporadic longitudinal study

questions.question: How does APOE modify CAA burden, hemorrhage, inflammation, and ARIA risk?
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: APOE contributes meaningful risk information in some contexts but is neither necessary nor sufficient.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Ancestry-diverse calibrated models with treatment interactions.
questions.decisive_design: Large prospective real-world registry linked to standardized MRI

questions.question: How accurately do clinicoradiologic criteria identify CAA-ri among realistic mimics?
questions.population: Adults with subacute encephalopathy, seizures, or asymmetric FLAIR lesions
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate

questions.critical_missing_piece: Prospective blinded study with infection, neoplasm, PRES, and vasculitis controls.
questions.decisive_design: Multicentre diagnostic cohort

questions.question: Which baseline and dynamic markers predict symptomatic or severe ARIA?
questions.index_or_exposure: Baseline CMB/cSS, APOE, dose, emerging imaging/fluid markers
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Known risk factors guide monitoring, but severe-event prediction remains limited.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Large prospective real-world treatment registry with harmonized serial MRI.
questions.decisive_design: Registry-based external model development and validation

questions.question: What is the temporal sequence from vascular dysfunction to nonhemorrhagic and hemorrhagic injury?
questions.population: Preclinical through symptomatic CAA and arteriolosclerosis
questions.index_or_exposure: Repeated physiology, barrier, diffusion, lesion, and amyloid measures
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: A staged framework is plausible, but individual-level transition evidence remains incomplete.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Dense longitudinal multimodal sampling beginning before symptoms.
questions.decisive_design: Hereditary-plus-sporadic natural-history platform

questions.question: Which combination best predicts hemorrhage, cognitive decline, disability, and death?
questions.index_or_exposure: Imaging, fluid, genetic, physiological, and clinical markers
questions.outcome: Calibration, competing risks, and net benefit
questions.timing: Cross-sectional and longitudinal components as appropriate
questions.current_answer: Several markers are prognostic, but unified externally calibrated models are uncommon.
questions.critical_missing_piece: Outcome-specific external validation and decision analysis.
questions.decisive_design: International prospective registry with locked models

questions.index_or_exposure: Imaging, physiological, fluid, and digital-pathology biomarkers

questions.current_answer: No arteriolosclerosis biomarker and few CAA biomarkers meet the full chain from repeatability to clinical surrogacy.

claims.claim: Impaired perivascular clearance contributes to CAA
claims.interpretation_supported: Clearance failure is a biologically coherent contributor and may participate in feedback with vascular amyloid
claims.not_established: That impaired outward flow is the initiating cause in sporadic human CAA or that MRI-visible PVS directly measure clearance
claims.key_limitation: Human direction and flux are not directly measured
claims.decisive_test: Longitudinal compartment-specific human transport measurement with regional temporal predictions

claims.claim: Vascular physiological dysfunction precedes hemorrhage in CAA
claims.interpretation_supported: Physiologic abnormalities plausibly occur before overt hemorrhagic lesions
claims.not_established: A universal temporal sequence or sufficient accuracy for preclinical diagnosis
claims.key_limitation: Sparse longitudinal sporadic CAA data
claims.decisive_test: Repeated CVR, perfusion, permeability, and lesion imaging in initially hemorrhage-free participants

claims.claim: BBB leakage is an early event in CAA vessel remodeling
claims.interpretation_supported: Leakage is detectable at mildly amyloid-positive vessels and is present in remodeled vessels
claims.not_established: That leakage initiates inflammation or rupture rather than reflecting concurrent injury
claims.key_limitation: Cross-sectional inference from seven autopsy cases
claims.decisive_test: Serial in vivo permeability followed by spatial whole-vessel pathology

claims.claim: A strictly lobar hemorrhagic pattern increases the probability of CAA
claims.interpretation_supported: Distribution is diagnostically informative in symptomatic populations when mimics and deep lesions are considered
claims.not_established: That every lobar CMB is caused by CAA or that performance transfers unchanged to screening populations
claims.key_limitation: Arteriolosclerosis can produce lobar CMBs and accuracy is spectrum-dependent
claims.decisive_test: Large lesion-level MRI-pathology coregistration across symptomatic and community cohorts

claims.claim: Severe centrum-semiovale PVS add information for CAA classification
claims.interpretation_supported: CSO-PVS can improve sensitivity when combined with hemorrhagic features in Boston v2.0
claims.not_established: That PVS are specific for CAA or directly quantify clearance
claims.key_limitation: Incremental value varies by population and rating method
claims.decisive_test: External pathology validation with arterial/venous mapping and prespecified thresholds

claims.claim: The multispot WMH pattern adds information for CAA classification
claims.interpretation_supported: The pattern can contribute to Boston v2.0 classification
claims.not_established: That it is a strong standalone or pathology-specific CAA marker
claims.key_limitation: Marginal incremental performance and limited direct validation
claims.decisive_test: Large blinded MRI-pathology study against arteriolosclerosis and mixed-pathology controls

claims.claim: Brain arteriolosclerosis is a heterogeneous family of vessel-wall changes
claims.interpretation_supported: Regional, morphologic, etiologic, and measurement heterogeneity should be represented explicitly
claims.not_established: A universally accepted molecular subtype system
claims.key_limitation: Routine semiquantitative grading collapses different lesions
claims.decisive_test: Multiregion molecular-spatial clustering with external replication

claims.claim: Brain arteriolosclerosis contributes independently to cognitive impairment
claims.interpretation_supported: Autopsy cohorts support an association after accounting for major co-pathologies
claims.not_established: A single pathway, a precise individual-level effect, or reversibility
claims.key_limitation: Residual confounding and measurement error in co-pathologies
claims.decisive_test: Prospective pathology-linked biomarkers with domain-specific cognitive slopes

claims.claim: Brain arteriolosclerosis is associated with hippocampal sclerosis/LATE-related pathology
claims.interpretation_supported: Repeated autopsy data support a multiregional association
claims.not_established: That arteriolosclerosis causes LATE-NC or hippocampal sclerosis
claims.key_limitation: Cross-sectional autopsy data cannot determine temporal direction
claims.decisive_test: Longitudinal vascular biomarkers followed by standardized LATE-NC pathology

claims.claim: Nonhemorrhagic tissue injury contributes importantly to cognition in CAA
claims.interpretation_supported: Diffusion, network, white-matter, and ischemic injury are plausible contributors beyond overt ICH
claims.not_established: Their independent causal proportion after AD, LATE, and arteriolosclerosis are fully controlled
claims.key_limitation: Co-pathology and mediation are incompletely measured
claims.decisive_test: Longitudinal multimodal change models with AD/LATE biomarkers and incident lesions

claims.claim: ARTS predicts pathology-linked arteriolosclerosis risk in older research cohorts
claims.interpretation_supported: ARTS shows approximately 0.8 discrimination under short MRI-death intervals in development/testing cohorts
claims.not_established: Clinical diagnostic accuracy in younger or representative populations, calibrated thresholds, or treatment responsiveness
claims.key_limitation: Small pathology test set and incomplete external pathology replication

claims.claim: Composite SVD scores summarize burden but do not identify etiology

claims.claim: Regional amyloid PET patterns may add differential information for CAA versus AD, but current evidence does not support standalone pathology-specific diagnosis

claims.claim: Spontaneous CAA-related inflammation and treatment-related ARIA share vascular-amyloid, permeability, and inflammatory features but are not interchangeable entities

claims.claim: Hereditary CAA is a powerful temporal and mechanistic model but does not automatically transport to sporadic late-life CAA

claims.claim: Blood biomarkers can index components of vascular injury but currently lack standalone specificity for CAA or brain arteriolosclerosis

claims.not_established: A validated single blood test for either target vessel pathology
claims.key_limitation: Construct overlap, assay heterogeneity, confounding, and few pathology-linked cohorts
claims.decisive_test: Blinded multisite pathology-linked plasma study with prespecified assays, competing pathologies, and incremental-value analysis

studies.population: Age >=50 with spontaneous ICH, cognitive impairment, or TFNE and MRI plus tissue
studies.setting: 10 North American and European academic centres
studies.index_test_or_exposure: Boston v2.0 MRI-clinical criteria
studies.reference_standard: Neuropathologic CAA assessment from biopsy, hematoma evacuation, or autopsy
studies.outcome: Probable CAA sensitivity, specificity, and AUC
studies.key_result: Derivation 74.8%/84.6%; temporal validation 92.5%/89.5%; geographic validation 80.2%/81.5%; full-autopsy subset 74.5%/95.0%, AUC 0.848
studies.major_limitations: Retrospective tissue-selected sample; heterogeneous tissue extent and clinical presentations; not validated as population screening
studies.applicability: Strongest for symptomatic referral populations resembling enrolled cases

studies.design: prospective population-based inception cohort; model development and diagnostic accuracy
studies.population: Adults with first-ever CT-diagnosed ICH who died and underwent research autopsy
studies.index_test_or_exposure: CT subarachnoid extension, finger-like projections, and APOE e4
studies.reference_standard: Masked standardized neuropathology
studies.outcome: CAA-associated lobar ICH
studies.key_result: Among 62 lobar ICH cases, 36 had moderate/severe CAA; three-variable model c-statistic 0.92; rule-in specificity 96%
studies.major_limitations: Only 62 lobar ICH cases; internal bootstrap validation; genotype may not be available; restricted to lobar ICH
studies.applicability: Applicable to acute lobar ICH evaluated by CT; not other CAA presentations

studies.population: Three patients meeting probable CAA during life but without CAA on routine neuropathology
studies.index_test_or_exposure: Lobar CMB location on in vivo, ex vivo 3T, and selected 7T MRI
studies.reference_standard: Serial histopathology of targeted lesions and culprit vessels
studies.outcome: Pathologic substrate of lobar CMBs
studies.key_result: Seven true CMB correlates were retrieved; culprit vessels showed moderate/severe arteriolosclerosis and no CAA; lesions tended toward juxtacortical/subcortical WM
studies.major_limitations: Extreme selected case series; only three patients and seven confirmed CMBs; localization hypothesis exploratory
studies.applicability: Demonstrates counterexamples, not frequency or diagnostic accuracy

studies.population: Autopsy cases with definite CAA and non-CAA controls
studies.index_test_or_exposure: In vivo/ex vivo MRI-visible PVS and segmented histologic EPVS
studies.reference_standard: Regional and single-vessel histopathology
studies.outcome: Association of EPVS with vascular amyloid and vessel-wall changes
studies.key_result: EPVS were mainly around WM portions of perforating cortical arterioles; burden associated with CAA severity in overlying cortex; affected vessels showed smooth-muscle loss and vascular amyloid
studies.major_limitations: 19 CAA and 5 controls; selected autopsy material; cross-sectional spatial association cannot establish flow direction
studies.applicability: Supports spatial biological plausibility; not standalone diagnostic accuracy

studies.short_name: BBB leakage and inflammation across CAA vessel grades
studies.population: Seven definite CAA cases: two MRI-targeted severe cases and five consecutive cases
studies.index_test_or_exposure: CAA vessel grade
studies.reference_standard: Immunohistochemistry for fibrin(ogen), SMA, GFAP, and CD68
studies.outcome: Vessel-wall leakage, smooth-muscle loss, inflammation, and remodeling
studies.key_result: Leakage and SMA loss were more frequent at mild amyloid grade than grade 0; all remodeled grade 3/4 vessels showed leakage; inflammation predominated later
studies.major_limitations: Seven cases; many vessel observations are not independent persons; temporal order inferred from cross-sectional grades
studies.applicability: Mechanistic hypothesis generation; not proof that leakage initiates rupture

studies.design: prediction model development, translation, and external cohort association
studies.population: Community-based older adults with ex vivo MRI/pathology plus separate in vivo test and cognitive cohorts
studies.n: 119 training; 79 pathology test; 369, 72, and 244 cognitive cohorts
studies.index_test_or_exposure: WMH, regional FA, age, and sex combined in automated ARTS score
studies.reference_standard: Semiquantitative autopsy arteriolosclerosis for diagnostic testing
studies.outcome: Pathology discrimination, reproducibility, and cognitive decline
studies.key_result: Mean ex vivo AUC 0.78; in vivo test AUC 0.79 when MRI-death interval <=2.4 years; scan-rescan ICC 0.99; higher score associated with decline in selected cognitive domains
studies.major_limitations: Small pathology samples; performance worsened with longer MRI-death interval; oldest-old cohorts; calibration and clinical thresholds not established
studies.applicability: Candidate research biomarker; not a clinical diagnostic test

studies.short_name: ARTS instrumental and clinical validation abstract
studies.population: Older adults in multisite technical datasets and Rush/ARIC cognitive cohorts
studies.index_test_or_exposure: Containerized ARTS score
studies.reference_standard: Technical repeatability/reproducibility; cognitive trajectories rather than pathology for clinical validation
studies.outcome: Inter-rater reliability, test-retest repeatability, inter-scanner reproducibility, and cognitive association
studies.key_result: ICC 0.9999 inter-rater, 0.996 test-retest, 0.955 inter-scanner; baseline ARTS associated with cognitive level and decline
studies.major_limitations: Supplement abstract rather than complete report; limited appraisal detail; cognitive association does not revalidate pathology specificity
studies.applicability: Strong technical signal; biological and clinical utility remain separate

studies.short_name: ARTS vascular risk and incident outcomes

studies.index_test_or_exposure: Baseline ARTS score
studies.reference_standard: Standard cohort adjudication of MCI, dementia, stroke, and vascular risks
studies.outcome: Incident MCI, dementia, stroke, and risk-factor associations
studies.key_result: Higher ARTS score was associated with incident MCI, dementia, stroke, and several vascular risk factors
studies.major_limitations: Observational associations; score includes age/sex and MRI injury features; outcome association does not prove arteriolosclerosis specificity or treatment responsiveness
studies.applicability: Supports prognostic association in older adults, not clinical diagnosis

studies.short_name: Arteriolosclerosis and hippocampal sclerosis of ageing
studies.design: multi-cohort autopsy association with digital pathology subset
studies.population: Autopsied adults age >=80 across UK-ADC, NACC, and Nun Study
studies.index_test_or_exposure: Regional semiquantitative arteriolosclerosis and vessel morphology
studies.reference_standard: Neuropathologic HS-ageing
studies.outcome: Association and vessel morphology

studies.major_limitations: Autopsy selection; historical semiquantitative ratings; cross-sectional association; HS-ageing terminology predates current LATE framework

diagnostic_profiles.name: Boston criteria v2.0
diagnostic_profiles.context: Etiologic classification of sporadic CAA in defined age/presentation contexts
diagnostic_profiles.technical_validity: Depends on high-quality hemorrhagic and nonhemorrhagic MRI marker rating
diagnostic_profiles.biological_validity: Markers are associated with CAA but are not individually pathognomonic
diagnostic_profiles.diagnostic_accuracy: Strongest in symptomatic tissue-selected cohorts; lower in community and nonhemorrhagic validations
diagnostic_profiles.prognostic_validity: Criteria category is not itself a complete outcome-risk model
diagnostic_profiles.incremental_value: Adds nonhemorrhagic markers over earlier versions; context-dependent
diagnostic_profiles.transportability: Limited outside populations resembling validation cohorts
diagnostic_profiles.clinical_utility: Useful diagnostic framework when applied within intended context
diagnostic_profiles.main_failure_mode: Spectrum effects, mixed pathology, inadequate MRI, and using criteria as universal screening
diagnostic_profiles.next_validation: Prospective presentation-specific external validation with full reference standard

diagnostic_profiles.name: ARTS
diagnostic_profiles.context: Research prediction of pathology-linked arteriolosclerosis risk
diagnostic_profiles.technical_validity: Promising repeatability evidence, including conference-level validation
diagnostic_profiles.biological_validity: Development linked MRI/demographic features to autopsy pathology
diagnostic_profiles.diagnostic_accuracy: Development AUC reported; independent external pathology accuracy not established
diagnostic_profiles.prognostic_validity: Associations with cognition and vascular outcomes reported
diagnostic_profiles.incremental_value: Not yet demonstrated against strong conventional baselines across independent cohorts
diagnostic_profiles.main_failure_mode: Conflating reproducibility or outcome association with diagnostic validation
diagnostic_profiles.next_validation: Locked independent MRI-autopsy validation with calibration and decision analysis

diagnostic_profiles.name: CVR MRI
diagnostic_profiles.context: Physiological measurement of vascular reserve in SVD/VCID
diagnostic_profiles.technical_validity: Multisite protocol evidence exists; acquisition and gas delivery remain demanding
diagnostic_profiles.biological_validity: Measures vascular responsiveness and predicts some structural progression
diagnostic_profiles.diagnostic_accuracy: No pathology-specific CAA or arteriolosclerosis threshold
diagnostic_profiles.prognostic_validity: Associated with cognition and one-year WMH/PVS progression; not all clinical outcomes
diagnostic_profiles.incremental_value: Needs comparison with conventional MRI and vascular risks
diagnostic_profiles.transportability: Promising across research sites; routine-care feasibility limited
diagnostic_profiles.main_failure_mode: Treating a general vascular-function signal as an etiologic diagnosis

diagnostic_profiles.name: Regional amyloid PET
diagnostic_profiles.context: Research differentiation of CAA, AD, and controls
diagnostic_profiles.biological_validity: Detects fibrillar amyloid but vascular/parenchymal compartment assignment is indirect
diagnostic_profiles.diagnostic_accuracy: Group-level regional differences; no validated universal patient threshold
diagnostic_profiles.incremental_value: Unclear beyond MRI and AD biomarkers
diagnostic_profiles.transportability: Limited by tracer, stage, and reference-standard heterogeneity
diagnostic_profiles.main_failure_mode: Calling amyloid positivity vascular CAA in an older person with AD
diagnostic_profiles.next_validation: Multi-tracer PET-to-autopsy study with mixed-pathology modeling

diagnostic_profiles.name: CAA-ri clinicoradiologic criteria
diagnostic_profiles.technical_validity: Requires appropriate FLAIR, susceptibility, diffusion, and often contrast imaging
diagnostic_profiles.biological_validity: Phenotype reflects inflammatory/permeability injury around amyloid-laden vessels
diagnostic_profiles.diagnostic_accuracy: Validated in selected cohorts; mimic-rich external performance remains uncertain
diagnostic_profiles.prognostic_validity: Not a complete treatment-response or relapse model
diagnostic_profiles.incremental_value: Can reduce unnecessary biopsy when syndrome and imaging align
diagnostic_profiles.transportability: Best in specialist contexts with alternative-diagnosis assessment
diagnostic_profiles.main_failure_mode: Missing infection, neoplasm, PRES, vasculitis, or therapy-associated ARIA
diagnostic_profiles.next_validation: Prospective blinded accuracy study including realistic mimics

diagnostic_profiles.name: Total SVD score
diagnostic_profiles.technical_validity: Simple and reproducible when component ratings are reliable
diagnostic_profiles.biological_validity: Combines downstream injury markers from potentially different etiologies
diagnostic_profiles.diagnostic_accuracy: Not intended to diagnose a vessel pathology
diagnostic_profiles.prognostic_validity: Associated with clinical and network outcomes in several cohorts
diagnostic_profiles.incremental_value: May summarize burden efficiently but can discard spatial and continuous information
diagnostic_profiles.transportability: Reasonable for burden comparisons with harmonized definitions
diagnostic_profiles.main_failure_mode: Interpreting a burden score as CAA or arteriolosclerosis
diagnostic_profiles.next_validation: Outcome-specific comparison with continuous and spatial measures

diagnostic_profiles.name: ARIA monitoring framework
diagnostic_profiles.technical_validity: Standardized serial MRI and communication are central
diagnostic_profiles.biological_validity: ARIA-E and ARIA-H reflect therapy-associated permeability/inflammatory and hemorrhagic injury
diagnostic_profiles.diagnostic_accuracy: Designed for treatment context, not spontaneous CAA diagnosis
diagnostic_profiles.prognostic_validity: Baseline markers inform risk; severe-event prediction remains limited
diagnostic_profiles.incremental_value: Provides operational safety value beyond unsystematic MRI review
diagnostic_profiles.clinical_utility: High within current treatment pathways using drug-specific guidance
diagnostic_profiles.main_failure_mode: Confusing ARIA with infarct, PRES, spontaneous CAA-ri, or other mimics
diagnostic_profiles.next_validation: Large real-world registry with standardized MRI and adjudicated severe outcomes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Perivascular clearance failure is an initiating driver of sporadic CAA
hypotheses.strongest_for: Anatomical plausibility, vascular amyloid distribution, hereditary/experimental models, and spatial PVS-pathology associations
hypotheses.strongest_against: Human flow direction and temporal onset are not directly established; clearance impairment may be secondary to vessel injury
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: Production, vessel affinity, age-related matrix change, pulsatility, and BBB dysfunction
hypotheses.falsifier: Normal direct clearance before and during early vascular amyloid accumulation despite sensitive measurement
hypotheses.decisive_experiment: Longitudinal compartment-specific human transport study beginning before imaging disease

hypotheses.hypothesis: Vascular physiological dysfunction precedes structural cSVD injury
hypotheses.strongest_for: Longitudinal CVR predicts later WMH/PVS progression; staged CAA frameworks place physiology before tissue injury
hypotheses.strongest_against: Reverse causation and shared vascular risks remain possible; clinical outcomes were not predicted at one year in MSS3
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: Existing microscopic tissue injury could impair measured reactivity
hypotheses.falsifier: Repeated normal physiology immediately before incident lesions in adequately powered cohorts
hypotheses.decisive_experiment: Repeated physiology and structural imaging with cross-lagged and intervention analyses

hypotheses.hypothesis: BBB leakage is an early causal amplifier of CAA vessel injury
hypotheses.strongest_for: Leakage and inflammation increase with histologic vessel injury and fit ARIA/CAA-ri biology
hypotheses.strongest_against: Human evidence is mainly cross-sectional and leakage can follow vessel damage
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: Inflammation, ischemia, and amyloid toxicity independently generate permeability
hypotheses.falsifier: No leakage before progression when measured serially with sensitive methods
hypotheses.decisive_experiment: Serial DCE-MRI/fluid markers with spatial pathology and treatment perturbation

hypotheses.hypothesis: A strictly lobar hemorrhagic pattern is sufficiently specific for CAA
hypotheses.strongest_for: Strong pathology-linked enrichment and established Boston criteria performance in symptomatic cohorts
hypotheses.strongest_against: Nonamyloid arteriolosclerosis can produce some lobar/juxtacortical microbleeds; performance falls in other spectra
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: Trauma, embolic lesions, vascular malformations, treatment effects, and mixed disease
hypotheses.falsifier: High rate of non-CAA pathology among rigorously localized strictly lobar lesions
hypotheses.decisive_experiment: Lesion-matched MRI-histology plus external diagnostic validation

hypotheses.hypothesis: CSO-PVS are an in-vivo marker of regional cortical CAA burden
hypotheses.strongest_for: Spatial MRI-pathology association with overlying cortical amyloid and smooth-muscle loss
hypotheses.strongest_against: PVS are common with aging and multiple SVD mechanisms; rating and causal interpretation vary
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: Atrophy, altered interstitial fluid, venous factors, and other small-vessel pathology
hypotheses.falsifier: No regional association in larger blinded pathology cohorts after confounding control
hypotheses.decisive_experiment: Multiregion MRI-autopsy mapping with reproducible automated PVS quantification

hypotheses.hypothesis: A deep/perforator MRI pattern can diagnose brain arteriolosclerosis
hypotheses.strongest_for: Biological plausibility and candidate associations of deep lesions, WMH, infarcts, diffusion, and vascular risks
hypotheses.strongest_against: No accepted pathology-validated criteria; lesions are downstream, mixed, and sequence-dependent
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: CAA, embolism, diabetes, aging, AD, inflammation, and other arteriopathies
hypotheses.falsifier: Poor external calibration against standardized multiregion pathology
hypotheses.decisive_experiment: Large derivation plus independent locked MRI-autopsy validation

hypotheses.strongest_for: Autopsy associations persist after adjustment in several aging cohorts
hypotheses.strongest_against: Residual confounding, measurement error, mediation by infarcts/WMH, and cohort reuse
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: ADNC, LATE, hippocampal sclerosis, frailty, and vascular risks
hypotheses.falsifier: No association after robust measurement-error and causal-pathway modeling across independent cohorts
hypotheses.decisive_experiment: Replicated longitudinal autopsy mediation analysis with harmonized pathology

hypotheses.hypothesis: ARTS is a valid in-vivo biomarker of arteriolosclerosis
hypotheses.strongest_for: Pathology-linked development, reported AUC, translation to in-vivo MRI, and repeatability work
hypotheses.strongest_against: Limited independent pathology validation, selected cohorts, and uncertain incremental utility
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: ARTS may reflect general aging, WMH/diffusion injury, or vascular risk burden
hypotheses.falsifier: Failure of locked calibration/discrimination in an independent MRI-autopsy cohort
hypotheses.decisive_experiment: Independent preregistered external pathology validation against strong baselines

hypotheses.hypothesis: CAA-ri and treatment-related ARIA lie on one inflammatory vascular-amyloid continuum
hypotheses.strongest_for: Overlapping ARIA-E/ARIA-H imaging, vascular amyloid, permeability, inflammation, and occasional clinicopathologic resemblance
hypotheses.strongest_against: Distinct triggers, treatment exposure, natural history, ascertainment, and incomplete direct comparative data
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: Shared downstream injury from different initiating mechanisms
hypotheses.falsifier: Consistently nonoverlapping immune, imaging, and pathology signatures in direct comparisons
hypotheses.decisive_experiment: Harmonized prospective CAA-ri versus ARIA multi-omic/imaging/pathology study

hypotheses.hypothesis: Regional amyloid PET can distinguish CAA from AD
hypotheses.strongest_for: Meta-analysis finds lower global CAA uptake than AD and relatively higher occipital-to-global uptake
hypotheses.strongest_against: Most reference diagnoses are clinical; AD co-pathology and tracer heterogeneity blur compartments
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: Disease stage, tracer affinity, atrophy, and mixed parenchymal/vascular amyloid
hypotheses.falsifier: No patient-level separation against compartment-specific autopsy pathology

hypotheses.hypothesis: A fluid biomarker panel can distinguish CAA from AD and arteriolosclerosis
hypotheses.strongest_for: Disease-related amyloid, neuronal, inflammatory, endothelial, and pericyte signals are detectable
hypotheses.strongest_against: Substantial construct overlap, assay heterogeneity, and little pathology-linked external validation
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: Systemic vascular disease, renal function, age, AD, and nonspecific neurodegeneration
hypotheses.falsifier: No incremental accuracy beyond clinical/MRI models in representative pathology cohorts
hypotheses.decisive_experiment: Locked multisite plasma/CSF panel tested against mixed autopsy pathology

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mixed CAA, arteriolosclerosis, and neurodegenerative pathology interact rather than merely add
hypotheses.strongest_for: Frequent co-occurrence, shared vascular/amyloid pathways, spatial vulnerability, and heterogeneous phenotypes
hypotheses.strongest_against: Interaction estimates are underpowered, scale-dependent, and vulnerable to measurement error
hypotheses.alternative_explanations: Independent additive effects plus age-related co-occurrence
hypotheses.falsifier: Consistently additive models with good calibration across independent cohorts and scales
hypotheses.decisive_experiment: Large replicated multiregion pathology-imaging cohort with prespecified interaction scales

use_cases.title: Lobar ICH with disseminated cSS
use_cases.scenario: An older adult presents with spontaneous lobar ICH, multiple strictly lobar microbleeds, and disseminated cSS.
use_cases.reasoning: The phenotype strongly increases CAA probability in the intended symptomatic context. Apply current criteria, confirm sequence adequacy, and separately estimate recurrence and treatment risk.
use_cases.do_not_conclude: Do not infer that every cognitive symptom is caused by CAA or that competing pathology is absent.

use_cases.title: Cognitive presentation without hemorrhage
use_cases.scenario: A memory-clinic patient has WMH, CSO-PVS, and no hemorrhagic marker.
use_cases.reasoning: Boston v2.0 transportability is weaker in this spectrum. Consider AD and mixed pathology, verify MRI quality, and treat any CAA inference as uncertain.
use_cases.do_not_conclude: Do not use criteria performance from lobar ICH cohorts as if it were screening performance.

use_cases.title: Mixed lobar and deep microbleeds
use_cases.scenario: MRI shows both lobar and deep microbleeds with extensive WMH.
use_cases.reasoning: Model mixed or competing pathologies. Fine-grained lesion location and cSS may help, but neither distribution alone supplies a pathology diagnosis.
use_cases.do_not_conclude: Do not force a binary CAA-versus-hypertensive label.

use_cases.title: High ARTS score
use_cases.scenario: A research participant has a high ARTS score and worsening cognition.
use_cases.reasoning: Separate model output, pathology prediction, technical repeatability, outcome association, and clinical utility. Inspect cohort similarity and calibration.
use_cases.do_not_conclude: Do not label the participant pathology-positive without validated context and reference evidence.

use_cases.title: Subacute encephalopathy with asymmetric FLAIR
use_cases.scenario: An older adult develops seizures and cognitive change with asymmetric parieto-occipital FLAIR hyperintensity and lobar microbleeds.
use_cases.reasoning: CAA-ri is important, but infection, neoplasm, PRES, vasculitis, and seizure-related change require assessment. Treatment exposure determines whether ARIA enters the differential.
use_cases.do_not_conclude: Do not equate an ARIA-E-like appearance with one etiology.

use_cases.title: Positive amyloid PET in suspected CAA
use_cases.scenario: An older patient with cognitive impairment has positive amyloid PET and a small lobar microbleed burden.
use_cases.reasoning: PET confirms fibrillar amyloid but not its vascular compartment. Integrate regional PET, tau/CSF, MRI pattern, and mixed-pathology probability.
use_cases.do_not_conclude: Do not call a positive scan diagnostic of CAA.

use_cases.title: Reduced CVR with WMH progression
use_cases.scenario: A research participant has low CVR and increasing WMH over one year.
use_cases.reasoning: This supports vascular dysfunction as a risk marker for tissue progression, while etiology and causal reversibility remain unresolved.
use_cases.do_not_conclude: Do not infer CAA or arteriolosclerosis specificity from CVR alone.

use_cases.title: Radiology-report candidate phenotype
use_cases.scenario: A report mentions WMH, chronic infarcts, and deep microbleeds without direct image review.
use_cases.reasoning: Use the report for candidate generation and triage. Confirm sequence availability, negation, image-level location, and pathology reference before model development.
use_cases.do_not_conclude: Do not turn report text into validated diagnostic criteria.

constructs.label: Observation
constructs.definition: A recorded signal on imaging, fluid assay, clinical examination, physiology, genetics, or tissue

constructs.label: Phenotype
constructs.definition: A reproducibly described pattern of observations

constructs.label: Target pathology
constructs.definition: The vessel-wall or tissue condition the investigation aims to identify

constructs.label: Mechanism
constructs.definition: A proposed causal process linking exposures, vessel injury, tissue injury, and outcomes

constructs.label: Biomarker
constructs.definition: A measured characteristic used for a defined context of use

constructs.label: Diagnostic criterion
constructs.definition: A rule estimating disease probability in a defined population and presentation

constructs.label: Reference standard
constructs.definition: The method used to determine target-condition status
constructs.must_not_be_equated_with: Perfect truth when sampling is incomplete

constructs.label: Outcome
constructs.definition: A future event or state the model seeks to predict or change

constructs.label: Clinical action
constructs.definition: A decision integrating evidence, values, alternatives, and competing risks
